key_terms.meaning: s(t) = A_c [1 + m cos(2π f_m t)] cos(2π f_c t), where A_c is carrier amplitude, m is modulation index, f_m is message frequency and f_c is carrier frequency.
m = A_m / A_c for tone modulation; A_m is message amplitude and A_c is carrier amplitude.
Frequency components at f_c − f_m and f_c + f_m created by modulation.
B_AM = 2 f_m for tone modulation; f_m is the highest message frequency.
P_t = P_c (1 + m²/2), where P_c is carrier power and m is modulation index.
s(t) = A_c m(t) cos(2π f_c t); the carrier is suppressed and only sidebands remain.
Multiply the received signal by cos(2π f_c t) and low-pass filter to recover the message.
B_SSB = f_m for a single-sideband signal, half the AM or DSB bandwidth.
Vestigial-sideband modulation sends one sideband plus a small vestige of the other sideband.
Uses a nonlinear device with v_o = a₀ + a₁ v_i + a₂ v_i² to create sum and difference frequencies.
Two nonlinear branches are subtracted so the carrier cancels and DSB-SC remains.
Diode, capacitor and resistor circuit that follows the envelope of an AM wave.
Demodulator that uses a synchronized local carrier; it works for DSB-SC and SSB.
Modulates at low power and then uses linear RF amplifiers to reach final power.
Modulates the final RF power amplifier at full power.
Mixes incoming RF with a local oscillator to a fixed intermediate frequency for filtering and gain.
Fixed frequency f_IF inside a superheterodyne receiver where selectivity and amplification are obtained.
Unwanted frequency f_img = f_LO + f_IF that also mixes to the same IF as the desired signal.
Frequency-division multiplexing assigns each message a separate frequency band.
Unused frequency gap between adjacent FDM channels that prevents overlap.

takeaways: AM adds a carrier to the message; the carrier carries no information but makes envelope detection simple.
The modulation index m sets sideband amplitude; AM bandwidth is 2f_m and total power is P_c(1 + m²/2).
DSB-SC removes the carrier, saving power but requiring coherent detection with a synchronized local carrier.
SSB sends one sideband and uses half the bandwidth of DSB; VSB keeps a small vestige so practical filters can be built.
Square-law and balanced modulators use nonlinear devices; the balanced connection cancels the carrier and gives DSB-SC.
An envelope detector is simple and cheap but fails for DSB-SC and for overmodulated AM with m > 1.
Low-level transmitters modulate before power amplification; high-level transmitters modulate the final RF stage and suit high-power AM broadcast.
A superheterodyne receiver converts every RF channel to a fixed IF, giving good selectivity and gain; image rejection is a key design issue.
FDM stacks messages in frequency; filters and guard bands separate channels without overlap.
bank_note: Long answers usually ask for a derivation, waveform or spectrum sketch, block diagram, and a comparison of bandwidth and power trade-offs across AM, DSB-SC, SSB and VSB.

bank.q: Define the modulation index of AM. Derive the expression for an AM wave and sketch its spectrum. Show that the bandwidth is 2f_m and the total power is P_c(1 + m²/2).
outline: Write the carrier and message expressions.
Form s(t) = A_c[1 + m cos(2π f_m t)] cos(2π f_c t).
Expand into carrier, upper sideband and lower sideband.
Identify sideband frequencies f_c ± f_m and amplitudes m A_c/2.
State bandwidth B_AM = 2f_m.
Compute power using average of cos² and state P_t = P_c(1 + m²/2).

bank.q: Explain DSB-SC modulation. Derive its spectrum and describe coherent detection with a block diagram.
outline: Write s(t) = A_c m(t) cos(2π f_c t).
Show that the spectrum has two sidebands and no carrier line.
Draw the modulator as a multiplier.
Draw coherent detector: multiplier, local carrier and low-pass filter.
Explain that local carrier must match frequency and phase.
State that DSB-SC saves carrier power but needs synchronization.

bank.q: Compare SSB and VSB modulation. Explain why VSB is used for television video transmission and state its bandwidth.
outline: Define SSB as one sideband only.
State B_SSB = f_m.
Define VSB as one sideband plus a small vestige of the other.
Explain that VSB relaxes filter steepness at low frequencies.
State VSB bandwidth is slightly more than f_m.
Mention television video as a common VSB application.

bank.q: Explain the square-law modulator and the balanced modulator. How does the balanced connection suppress the carrier?
outline: Describe square-law device with v_o = a₀ + a₁v_i + a₂v_i².
Apply carrier plus message and identify sum and difference terms.
Show that a square-law modulator gives AM with carrier.
Draw balanced modulator with two nonlinear branches.
Subtract the two outputs to cancel carrier and a₀ terms.
State that the result is DSB-SC.

bank.q: Describe the envelope detector with a circuit diagram and waveforms. State the conditions for good detection.
outline: Draw diode, capacitor and resistor circuit.
Explain charging on positive half-cycle and discharging through R.
Choose RC time constant between message period and carrier period.
Show output follows the AM envelope.
State condition m ≤ 1 to avoid negative peak clipping.
Mention that diode drop and load affect weak-signal detection.

bank.q: Draw the block diagram of a superheterodyne receiver and explain the RF amplifier, mixer, local oscillator, IF amplifier and detector.
outline: Draw antenna, RF amplifier, mixer, local oscillator, IF amplifier, detector and audio output.
Explain that mixer translates RF to fixed IF.
State that IF filters give selectivity.
Explain local oscillator tuning.
Mention image frequency and image rejection.
State why fixed IF simplifies gain and filtering.

bank.q: Explain frequency-division multiplexing with transmitter and receiver block diagrams. Give an example using three voice channels and guard bands.
outline: Assign each message a carrier and a frequency slot.
Draw parallel modulators, bandpass filters and summing bus at transmitter.
Draw bandpass filters and demodulators at receiver.
Explain guard bands prevent overlap.
Use three 4 kHz voice channels as example.
State bandwidth includes channel widths plus guard bands.

bank.q: An AM transmitter radiates 10 kW with modulation index m = 0.6. Calculate the carrier power and the power in each sideband. If m is increased to 1, find the new total power.
outline: Use P_t = P_c(1 + m²/2).
Solve P_c = P_t / (1 + m²/2) = 10 kW / 1.18.
Compute P_c ≈ 8.47 kW.
Sideband power total is P_t − P_c ≈ 1.53 kW.
Each sideband is half of that, about 0.76 kW.

bank.q: A DSB-SC signal s(t) = 4 cos(2π × 10^6 t) cos(2π × 5 × 10^3 t) is applied to a coherent detector with local carrier 2 cos(2π × 10^6 t). Find the output after the low-pass filter.
outline: Multiply s(t) by 2 cos(2π × 10^6 t).
Use cos A cos B = ½[cos(A−B) + cos(A+B)].
Obtain a baseband term and a term near 2 × 10^6 Hz.
Low-pass filter removes the high-frequency term.
Output is proportional to 4 cos(2π × 5 × 10^3 t).
Mention that phase error reduces amplitude.

bank.q: Design an FDM scheme for four 4 kHz audio channels using DSB-SC with carrier frequencies 100 kHz, 110 kHz, 120 kHz and 130 kHz. Find the total bandwidth and the guard bands.
outline: Each DSB-SC channel occupies 8 kHz around its carrier.
Channel bands are 96–104 kHz, 106–114 kHz, 116–124 kHz and 126–134 kHz.
Guard bands are 2 kHz between adjacent channels.
Total occupied band is 96 kHz to 134 kHz.
Total bandwidth is 38 kHz.
State that filters at transmitter and receiver must separate these bands.

bank.q: Compare low-level and high-level AM transmitters. Explain linearity and efficiency trade-offs, and choose one for a 50 kW AM broadcast transmitter.
outline: Draw low-level transmitter: oscillator, modulator, linear RF amplifiers.
Draw high-level transmitter: RF oscillator, RF driver, final modulated stage.
Low-level needs linear amplifiers but modulation is easy at low power.
High-level is more efficient for high power but needs a high-power modulator.
Linearity affects distortion and splatter.
For 50 kW broadcast, high-level modulation is normally preferred.

bank.q: Evaluate envelope detection and coherent detection for AM with m > 1 and for DSB-SC. Which detector works, which fails, and why?
outline: Envelope detector follows positive envelope.
For m > 1, envelope crosses zero and detector distorts or clips.
For DSB-SC, envelope is |m(t)| and detector does not recover sign.
Coherent detector multiplies by local carrier and low-pass filters.
Coherent detection works for DSB-SC and SSB.
Phase and frequency errors in local carrier cause distortion or loss.

bank.q: Analyze the effect of increasing the AM modulation index from 0.3 to 1 on sideband power, bandwidth and transmitter rating. Comment on the practical limit.
outline: Sideband power fraction is m²/(2 + m²).
At m = 0.3, sideband power is small.
At m = 1, sideband power is one-third of total power.
Bandwidth remains 2f_m and does not change with m.
Transmitter must handle higher total power at m = 1.
m is kept at or below 1 to avoid overmodulation distortion.

bank.q: Evaluate a superheterodyne receiver for image rejection and selectivity. Explain how the choice of IF and RF filter affects performance.
outline: Image frequency is f_img = f_LO + f_IF.
A high IF makes image separation larger and eases RF filtering.
A low IF gives better selectivity with practical IF filters.
RF filter must reject the image before mixing.
Double conversion can improve image rejection.
Trade-off exists between image rejection and adjacent-channel selectivity.

glossary.def: Modulation in which the amplitude of a carrier is varied in proportion to the message.
High-frequency sinusoid that carries the message through a communication channel.
Message or information signal that changes a parameter of the carrier.
Ratio m = A_m/A_c for tone AM; it sets the sideband amplitude.
Frequency component at f_c ± f_m produced by modulation.
Frequency component at f_c + f_m.
Frequency component at f_c − f_m.
Range of frequencies occupied by a signal; AM bandwidth is 2f_m.
Double-sideband suppressed-carrier modulation; two sidebands and no carrier.
Demodulation by multiplying with a locally generated carrier of correct frequency and phase.
Oscillator in a receiver or detector that generates a reference carrier or mixing frequency.
Single-sideband modulation; transmits one sideband only.
Vestigial-sideband modulation; transmits one sideband plus a small part of the other.
Small remaining portion of the unwanted sideband in VSB.
Modulator using a device whose output has a squared term in the input voltage.
Modulator with two nonlinear branches whose outputs are subtracted to cancel the carrier.
Demodulator that follows the envelope of an AM wave using a diode and RC load.
Simple envelope detector using a diode, capacitor and resistor.
Modulation done at low power before linear RF amplification.
Modulation done at the final high-power RF amplifier.
Receiver that mixes incoming RF to a fixed intermediate frequency for filtering and amplification.
Fixed frequency used inside a superheterodyne receiver after mixing.
Unwanted frequency that also mixes to the same IF as the desired RF.
Frequency-division multiplexing; separate messages occupy separate frequency bands.
Unused frequency gap that prevents overlap between adjacent FDM channels.
Nonlinear circuit that combines RF and local oscillator to produce sum and difference frequencies.
